course_description: A project focusing on the information system plan brought about in the practicum / on-the-job training / independent research course. This course requires the fulfillment of the complete documentation and oral defense before a set of panelists.

course_learning_outcomes.text: Understand the latest concepts in systems analysis and design, software engineering and information technology.
Investigate and evaluate prominent literature connected to your Capstone Project. 1
Understand the scope of the project, planning, scheduling the collaborative efforts of the team, and documenting the effort via oral and written proposals.
Illustrate that they can function, communicate, collaborate and continue to learn effectively as ethically and socially responsible IT professionals.
Adapt the skills to communicate with and balance the interests of multiple stakeholders (both technical and non-technical) on a project.
Demonstrate 21st century skills in all learning activities.

topic_learning_outcomes.text: Identify complex problems and define the computing requirements appropriate to its solution.
Identify the user needs and consider them in the selection, creation, and evaluation and administration of computer-based systems.
Select various high level and detailed design and implementation principles for building a software system.
Analyze the impact of computing and engineering solutions on individuals, organizations, and society.
Identify software development needs and challenges that require various engineering solutions, and formulate such solutions
Execute effectively as a member or leader of a development team recognizing the different roles of a team to accomplish a common goal.
Understand professional, ethical, legal, security and social issues and responsibilities in the utilization of information technology.
Communicate effectively with the computing community and with society at large about complex computing activities through logical writing, presentations, and clear instructions.
Collaboration, Skilled Communication, Knowledge Construction, Self-Regulation, Real-World Problem- Solving, Use of ICT (not part of topic, but integrated in assessments)
